title: Draw the frame: int and long locals
prompt:
The program is paused inside `tally`, which keeps an int, a long and another int in its frame. Fill in where each one sits.

Each local's offset is an equate at the top of the program, built from the one before it. A long starts on a multiple of 8, so `sum_s` rounds up past a gap, and `alloc` rounds the whole frame up to a multiple of 16. Work each number out by hand and give it in bytes from fp, the way the frames view counts them.

## What is checked

- the frame's size in bytes
- the offsets from fp of `count_s`, `sum_s` and `last_s`
- the offsets from fp of the saved fp and the saved lr

Check runs the program to the pause and compares each number with the frame the emulator draws there. A wrong number shows a hint, never the answer.
program:
// Count the odd values in a list, add them up, and keep the last one found.

define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

count_size = 4                                  // int
sum_size = 8                                    // long
last_size = 4                                   // int

count_s = 16
sum_s = (count_s + count_size + 7) & -8         // a long starts on a multiple of 8
last_s = sum_s + sum_size
alloc = -(last_s + last_size) & -16
dealloc = -alloc

.data
values:     .word 12, 7, 30, 5, 19, 8
fmt_out:    .string "%d odd values, sum %ld, last %d\n"

.text

// tally(x0 = values, w1 = n): prints how many are odd, their sum and the last one
        .balign 4
        .global tally
tally:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, alloc]!
        mov     fp, sp

        str     wzr, [fp, count_s]              // count = 0
        str     xzr, [fp, sum_s]                // sum = 0
        str     wzr, [fp, last_s]               // last = 0

        mov     x9, x0                          // copy the arguments out of x0 and w1
        mov     w10, w1
        mov     w11, 0                          // index
        b       ta_test
ta_loop:
        ldr     w12, [x9, w11, SXTW 2]          // w12 = values[index]
        tst     w12, 1
        b.eq    ta_next                         // even: skip it
        ldr     w13, [fp, count_s]
        add     w13, w13, 1
        str     w13, [fp, count_s]              // count = count + 1
        sxtw    x14, w12
        ldr     x13, [fp, sum_s]
        add     x13, x13, x14
        str     x13, [fp, sum_s]                // sum = sum + value
        str     w12, [fp, last_s]               // last = value
ta_next:
        add     w11, w11, 1
ta_test:
        cmp     w11, w10
        b.lt    ta_loop

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        ldr     w1, [fp, count_s]
        ldr     x2, [fp, sum_s]
        ldr     w3, [fp, last_s]
        bl      printf

        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], dealloc
        ret

        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =values
        mov     w1, 6
        bl      tally

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret

slots.name: count_s
slots.hint: count_s is given as a plain number in the program.

slots.name: sum_s
slots.hint: Work out (count_s + count_size + 7) & -8 with count_s = 16 and count_size = 4: it rounds the end of count_s up to the next multiple of 8.

slots.name: last_s
slots.hint: last_s starts right where sum_s ends: sum_s + sum_size.

hints.size: The stp moves sp down by -alloc bytes, and that is the whole frame. Add up to the end of last_s (last_s + last_size), then round up to the next multiple of 16.
hints.savedFp: stp fp, lr, [sp, alloc]! stores fp first, at the new sp, and mov fp, sp then points fp at that same address.
hints.savedLr: lr is the second of the two registers the stp stores, in the bytes right after the saved fp.
